name: Sonnet concentrated AI/technology
strategy: Concentrated long book in AI infrastructure leaders (GPU compute, hyperscale cloud, networking silicon, memory) sized by relative-strength conviction this week, with cash held for weekly rebalancing flexibility.
reassessment_note: All five names reported/confirmed fundamentals this week and the tape sorted them clearly. NVDA printed a Q2 beat ($96.2B rev, $89B from data centers, Q3 guide $108B), closed the Hugging Face acquisition, and still screens cheap vs. AI-software peers on P/E with a $327 average street target against a $230 mark -- I am adding to it. AMD confirmed accelerating data-center momentum (+107% data-center revenue) and jumped 4.7% on Sept 4 with a fresh Raymond James target hike to $641 -- adding modestly. MSFT is the weak link this week: down 2% on Sept 4, fresh OpenAI-training lawsuits from Seattle Times/Newsday adding legal overhang, and Nadella disclosed a $43M pre-arranged sale; Stifel still lifted its target to $530 but kept only a Hold, so I am trimming size while keeping it the largest single name given the Azure AI capex buildout (31 new data centers) is real. AVGO beat Q3 revenue (+86% y/y) but guided $34.8B vs. a $35B consensus and sold off on the miss-to-whisper; Hock Tan's public confidence in AI-compute demand through 2028 keeps me holding the position unchanged rather than adding into the guidance disappointment. MU ripped +6.1% on the strong August jobs print and rides a +256% YTD move, but David Tepper trimming 41% of his stake is a valuation caution flag, so I am sizing it up only slightly. Net effect: rotate weight from the MSFT overhang into the NVDA/AMD momentum leaders, leave AVGO and cash untouched, nudge MU. Cash stays at 18% for flexibility into next week's CPI print.

positions.thesis: Q2 beat with $89B data-center revenue and a $108B Q3 guide confirms the compute buildout is not slowing; the $12.9B Hugging Face acquisition extends NVIDIA's grip on the open-source model ecosystem/software layer. Trading at a discount to AI-software peers on P/E with a $327 average target vs. $230 mark gives the best risk/reward of the book -- sizing up to the largest single-name weight.

Azure AI capex (31 new data centers) and enterprise Copilot attach remain the core secular driver, but this week added real overhang: fresh OpenAI-training lawsuits from major newspapers, a $43M Nadella insider sale, and a 2% down day into a Stifel target hike that still only rates it Hold. Trimming from 30% to 22% to reflect the near-term legal/sentiment risk while keeping meaningful exposure to the cloud-AI franchise.

Q3 revenue grew 86% y/y but the $34.8B guide missed the $35B whisper, driving a post-print selloff. Leaving size unchanged rather than adding into the guidance disappointment or cutting into a name where custom-ASIC/networking demand (per CEO commentary on AI compute demand through 2028) is still structurally intact.

Data-center revenue +107% y/y and a 4.7% single-day rally on Sept 4 with a Raymond James target hike to $641 shows the MI-series ramp gaining street credibility even while the stock sits 19% below its 52-week high -- adding to size to capture the re-rating.

HBM/DRAM pricing cycle plus the strong August jobs print drove a +6.1% day and a +256% YTD move; David Tepper trimming 41% of his position is a real caution signal on how extended the move is, so keeping this the smallest position in the book rather than chasing it further.
